# The decoders of LOCAL bytes: compressed streams, filesystem images, image
# formats. Swept by .github/workflows/vuln.yml on `workflow_dispatch` ONLY --
# there is no cron over this list, and that is a measured decision rather than
# an omission.
#
# ⛔ WHY NOT NIGHTLY: GitHub rate limits the git transport. Measured 2026-10-31,
# same binary, same toolchain, runs an hour apart:
#
#   13 repositories (vulnscan-tools.txt)     read clean, twice
#   22 repositories (tools + exposed)        22 scanned, 0 UNREAD
#   58 repositories (tools' population + all of these)
#                                            14 of 58 UNREAD, every failure a
#                                            `git clone … 403` -- and my own
#                                            push was refused the same way
#
# UNREAD is not clean: vulnscan exits 2, so a nightly sweep of this list would
# make the lane RED for a reason that is the sweep's own and not any
# repository's -- the exact shape of alarm this workflow was written to refuse.
#
# ⛔ AND SLICING IT ACROSS THE WEEK WAS THE WRONG ANSWER. It keeps everything in
# view and reintroduces the latency the clock exists to remove: an advisory
# published on Monday would reach Friday's slice on Friday, and the founding
# case here is two advisories found 2 and 4 days late.
#
# So the nightly budget goes to EXPOSURE (see vulnscan-exposed.txt), which is
# where reachability actually was: both repositories that reached an advisory
# among all 58 were network-facing. These decode a byte slice somebody already
# has, which is a smaller surface and no transport dependency.
#
# ⛔ WHAT WOULD MAKE THEM NIGHTLY, so the next reader does not re-derive it:
# authenticated clones (which gives up the no-credential property this job is
# built on -- it makes no REST call per repository, so it cannot starve the
# budget the Renovate runners spend from), or a run that stays under roughly
# two dozen clones. `-state` with `-retry-unread` belongs INSIDE whichever is
# chosen -- it makes one run resumable, 14 retries instead of 58 -- but it must
# NOT be carried between nights: a repository that was CLEAN yesterday is not
# clean today if an advisory was published since. The code does not change; the
# database does, which is the whole reason this runs on a clock.
#
# ⛔ RUN IT BY HAND after any x/net, x/crypto or stdlib advisory lands, and
# before trusting a silence from it. A dispatch-only lane reports nothing when
# nobody asks, and nothing is not green.
#
# Last full pass: 2026-10-31, 58 scanned, 56 clean, 2 reaching GO-2026-6860 --
# both network-facing, both now fixed, and both now in vulnscan-exposed.txt.
